challenges.title: Six words
challenges.description: Write a complete micro-story in exactly six words.
tips: Count your words at the end, not while writing: write first.
A six-word story suggests far more than it tells.
Aim for an implied beginning and end, leave the middle to the reader.

challenges.title: A letter to your future self
challenges.description: Write a few lines to the person you'll be in ten years.
tips: Open with a simple hello, like writing to a friend, it unblocks you instantly.
Write about the present, that's what will matter most in ten years.
Nobody will read this, you can be completely honest.

challenges.title: A color without naming it
challenges.description: Describe a color of your choice without ever naming it.
tips: Go through the senses: temperature, taste, texture, sound.
Name objects that have the colour without ever naming the colour.
Reread to catch the forbidden word if it slipped in.

challenges.title: Overheard at a café
challenges.description: Imagine a conversation between two strangers you might have overheard at a café.
tips: Write only the lines, don't describe the characters.
Start in the middle of the conversation, never with a greeting.
Real conversations are full of hesitations and unfinished sentences.

challenges.title: The door had been left open...
challenges.description: Write the opening of a story that begins with: "The door had been left open..."
tips: Don't worry about meaning: write the next sentence, then the next.
Decide quickly who finds the door, everything else follows from that.
You can stop mid-suspense, this is only a beginning.

challenges.title: Three things you noticed today
challenges.description: Write down three things you noticed today, each in a single sentence.
tips: Go concrete: a light, a sound, someone's gesture.
One sentence, full stop: resist the urge to elaborate.
The most ordinary things make the best notes.

challenges.title: Haiku for right now
challenges.description: Write a haiku (5-7-5 syllables) about your mood right now.
tips: Count syllables on your fingers, line by line: 5, 7, 5.
A haiku usually speaks of a season or one precise moment.
If a syllable spills over, change the word rather than the structure.

challenges.title: Ten words you love
challenges.description: List ten words you love, no explanation needed.
tips: Write them as they come, no order, no logic.
The sound of a word is reason enough, it doesn't have to be beautiful.
If you stall at seven, look around you and steal three more.

challenges.title: A memory tied to a smell
challenges.description: Describe a memory tied to a specific smell.
tips: Start from the smell itself before getting to the memory.
The place and the people almost always come with the smell.
It doesn't need to be a big memory, a kitchen smell is enough.

challenges.title: Postcard
challenges.description: Write a postcard to someone you haven't seen in a long time.
tips: Space is limited: get to the point in the first line.
Tell one thing, not everything you've been doing.
You don't have to send it, write it for yourself first.

challenges.title: An everyday sound
challenges.description: Describe precisely a sound you heard today, without saying where it came from.
tips: Pick an ordinary sound: a door, a kettle, footsteps in the hallway.
Use concrete words rather than elaborate comparisons.
Let the reader guess the source from your description.

challenges.title: An object's life
challenges.description: Pick an object around you and imagine, in a few lines, everything it went through before ending up there.
tips: An ordinary object (a mug, a key) works better than a precious one.
No need to tell it all, one or two episodes are enough.
End on how it ended up with you.

challenges.title: A confident lie
challenges.description: Write a clearly false statement, then defend it as if it were true.
tips: The more absurd the starting statement, the more fun the exercise.
Take a very serious tone to defend it, the contrast makes it work.
You don't need to be convincing, just fully commit.

challenges.title: A recipe for the intangible
challenges.description: Write the recipe for something without ingredients: courage, patience, a rainy Sunday.
tips: Keep the structure of a real recipe: ingredients, then steps.
Pick an abstract word that speaks to you right now.
Absurd quantities (a pinch of doubt, three spoonfuls of silence) work well.

challenges.title: A letter to your younger self
challenges.description: Write a few lines to the person you were as a child.
tips: No need to aim for a specific age, pick whichever memory comes first.
Tell them one thing you wish you'd known back then.
The tone can be tender, funny, or both.

challenges.title: A place in sound alone
challenges.description: Describe a place you know well using only the sounds heard there.
tips: Don't mention what you see, only what you hear.
List the sounds in the order they come to mind.
A busy place (a kitchen, a street) gives you more to work with.

challenges.title: The rest of a dream
challenges.description: Continue a dream, yours or an invented one, from the point where it fades in your memory.
tips: If you don't remember a specific dream, invent a one-line start and carry on.
Dreams don't need to make sense, give yourself that freedom.
Stop as soon as it feels forced, the ending can stay open.

challenges.title: A word that doesn't exist
challenges.description: Invent a word and write its definition, as if it appeared in the dictionary.
tips: A word that sounds good out loud often helps you find its meaning.
Think of a feeling or situation that has no word for it yet.
Add an example sentence, like a real dictionary entry.

challenges.title: One extra day
challenges.description: Write what you'd do if tomorrow lasted forty-eight hours instead of twenty-four.
tips: Start with the first extra hour, precisely.
Mix practical things and pointless things, both count.
End on what you'd do very last.

challenges.title: Message in a bottle
challenges.description: Write a message as if you were sealing it in a bottle and throwing it into the sea, for a stranger.
tips: You don't know who'll read it, address it to someone imaginary.
Give one concrete detail about where you are right now.
End with a question for whoever finds it.
